Revenue

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following prayer:
"to issue a writ more particularly in the nature of writ of Mandamus directing the respondents herein to pay the compensation for acquired land to the extent of Ac.1.25 cents situated in Sy No.31 old corresponding to Sy No. 31/4/1/1, New of Ramai Village Mandal and District Adilabad which was acquired for the purpose of excavating distribution No.5 to the left canal of Sathnala Project and consequently declare the action of respondents in not paying the said compensation to the petitioner is illegal, arbitrary violative of Article 14, 21, 31A and 300 A of the Constitution of India and against the mandatory provisions of L.A. Act and to pass orders".
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the pattedar of agricultural land to the extent of Ac.5.80 cents situated in Sy No.31 (old) corresponding to Sy No.31/4/1/1,
(New) of Ramai Village, Mandal and Adilabad.

The respondents are acquired Ac.1.25 cents of the land of the petitioner in the year, 1998 for excavation of work of distribution of No.5 of left canal of Sathnala Project, without following due process of law.
Thereafter, the petitioner issued legal notice to the respondents on 13.03.1998.
In response to the same, the respondent No.4 herein through letter dated 03.04.1998 requested respondent No.1 for payment of compensation to the acquired land.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that in view of the representation of the petitioner,
the respondent No.1 herein addressed a letter dated 03.10.2007 to the respondent No.4, for detailed report.

Then the respondent No.4 addressed a letter to the respondent No.1 on 16.10.2007,
requested for conducting a joint inspection.
Thereafter the Tahsildar, Adilabad, addressed a letter dated 08.12.2007, requesting the respondent No.3 to attend a spot inspection on 12.12.2007.

The respondent No.1 directed the respondent No.4 to submit a report on 01.01.2009, inspite of that no action has been taken by the respondents, the petitioner constrained to file the present writ petition requesting to direct the respondents to pay the land acquisition compensation to the petitioner.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, basing on the counter filed by respondent Nos.1 and 2 submits that after following due procedure, the land acquisition award was passed for Survey No.31 to an extent of Ac.30.29 cents situated at Ramai Village Mandal, Adilabad District and as there is no title disputes, the compensation amount awarded @ Rs.7,500/- per Acre.

sentences.text: In Sy.No.31/3 to the extent of Ac.0.28 guntas acquired and amount paid to Sri Sajjanapu Ramulu and the petitioner is not having any right.
Taking into consideration of all the formalities, the joint inspection of the land etc, cannot be considered, there is no valid grounds in the writ petition and requested to dismiss the same.

5. After hearing both sides and perused the record, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner questioning in action of the respondents in not paying land acquisition compensation for the land acquired by the respondents without following due process of law, for the land to an extent Ac.1.25 cents situated in Sy.No.31 old corresponding to Sy No.31/4/1/1, New of Ramai Village Mandal, Adilabad District from 1998 onwards.

There is a lot of correspondence between the petitioner and, the respondents and finally on 01.01.2009, the respondent No.1 directed the respondent No.4 to conduct spot enquiry and submit report to solve the dispute, in view of the representation of the petitioner.
The respondent in their counter not given any answers with regard to the correspondence between them.

But it is clearly shows that the petitioner approached number of times with the respondents and the respondent Nos.1 and 2 were addressed letters to each other for conducting enquiry, but the same was not done by the respondents.

As per their correspondence,
the respondent Nos.1, 3 and 4 has to conduct survey and spot inspection in the presence of the petitioner with regard to the acquisition of land of the petitioners and after conducting enquiry if necessary, the respondents have to initiate land acquisition proceedings as per law for the payment of land acquisition compensation to the petitioner.

6. In view of the above findings, this writ petition is disposed of, directing the respondent No.1, 3 and 4 to conduct joint survey in the presence of the petitioner, if they found that land of the petitioner is under acquisition, they have to initiate land acquisition proceedings for payment of land acquisition compensation of the petitioner within four (4) months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.
No costs Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE K.SARATH Date:15.04.2024
